main_learning: Setting up templates, quality gates, a content plan and a safety check before research starts makes it easier to stay consistent and keep public/private boundaries clear.
Re-validating bounty programs directly against the live Immunefi page, and re-checking the full in-scope asset list carefully, avoids missing newer scope additions.

When a target has multiple third-party audits covering different subsystems at different times, check whether your cloned commit is before or after each report's fixed-version commit, rather than assuming the latest clone is fully post-fix everywhere.

'Temporary freezing of funds' can sit at Medium or High depending on a program's specific severity table, not just the generic Immunefi category name; worth checking that table explicitly when framing severity.

When re-checking prior audit items against your current commit, a version-control diff of just that cluster between the audit's reviewed commit and your commit is a fast first step: an empty diff turns a fresh re-read into a quick 'does the description still match the code' check.

When extending a component inventory toward full scope coverage, tracing how a newly-read component is wired into the already-covered cluster — even if it produces no new hypothesis — either surfaces something new or gives a defensible 'no drift' confirmation of an already-ruled-out item.

Separating an external findings corpus into two levels — concrete findings and generalized checks — lets an audit agent answer both 'what does this bug look like in practice?' and 'what should I always verify for this sector?'; mixing them into one format loses the distinction.

Re-validating scope at the end of an onboarding week (not just at the start) catches any asset additions that happened during the research window; a 5-minute check before the weekly retrospective is cheaper than discovering a missed in-scope contract mid-audit.

Finishing a structured course is a clean forcing function: it draws a line between preparation and active research. The skills that transfer are the ones applied immediately on a real target, not the ones filed away for later.
Before submitting on a path asymmetry in perpetuals protocols, the question is not whether the paths differ but whether the difference creates loss from the vault or only from the trader.
Reading protocol docs alongside contract source for the same component is more efficient than reading them sequentially; mismatches between spec and implementation are where findings live.
Reading two contracts back-to-back with the same invariant-focused lens produces structured candidates directly, without a separate analysis pass.
Writing a Foundry test skeleton before the implementation forces you to think about the preconditions explicitly. If you cannot write a realistic setup, the invariant is probably under-specified.

In a batched async redeem execution, caching the share price once before the loop is both a gas optimization and a consistency property: all requests in the same batch are settled at the same price regardless of how many internal calls happen.
FOUNDRY_FUZZ_RUNS controls fuzz test runs; FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_RUNS controls invariant test runs. They are independent and both must be set when increasing depth in a suite that uses both.

An invariant suite tells you what the protocol guarantees; adversarial mapping tells you what assumptions those guarantees rest on. For each invariant the useful question is: what would a caller need to be able to do to break this?
A weekly retrospective written on the last day of the research week keeps both the what-worked judgment and the plan-for-next-week accurate, because both require context that fades over the weekend.

Reading the target deposit path on a Saturday bridge session is productive when the goal is structural mapping rather than adversarial hunting: you arrive Monday with the handler extension scoped, not context-switching mid-session.
Reserving a Sunday session for metrics admin (weekly CSV, dashboard, contribution log) prevents Monday's research window from being spent on housekeeping rather than investigation.
An entrance fee that records value owed instead of minting fee shares keeps share accounting simpler and removes a second dilution path.
Do not guard an adversarial fuzzer action with the same preconditions the production path enforces, or the fuzzer never reaches the states worth attacking.
When a value conversion chains two sequential divisions, confirm each one floors on its own; a single combined check can hide a direction change between the steps.
When a fee floors a share amount and both the fee and the remainder round down, the dust lands on one side; trace which before calling the rounding conservative.
At the end of a rounding study the useful artifact is the per-property coverage table, not a bare no-leak-found; the reasoned-only rows are the to-do list.
The reasoned-only rows in a coverage table are a to-do list, not documentation; promote them to committed tests or mark them open.
Fee accounting is easy to test on the way up; the decrease and claim paths need their own fuzzer actions or they never get exercised.
Isolated state-machine tests prove a guard for one transition; only interleaving them under a fuzzer proves it holds against every ordering.
Atomicity of a batch is often a property of the platform revert semantics, not the loop body; a loop with no external calls settles all or nothing for free.
A loop summing independent per-item conversions is order-independent for free, but only if each item reads the same snapshot price and carries no remainder forward.
When a checklist says evaluate mechanism X and no such surface exists, record the absence as a scope fact instead of building a mock that proves nothing.
Reserving a Sunday slot for metrics and dashboard admin keeps Monday's research window for investigation rather than housekeeping.
A property that lives only in a journal is not a committed test; closing a week by diffing the journal against the suite catches the gap.
Signed integer division truncates toward zero, so one pro-rata formula rounds a credit and a debt in opposite economic directions.
A rounding bias is only exploitable if an untrusted party controls both the inputs and the instant the value is sampled.
Two inputs to the same permissionless call can be held to different freshness gates; find and test the weaker one.
Find the binding one of two subtractions by bounding the operands; a check that is redundant with an earlier one is not an independent risk.
A short weekend admin pass reconciling the metrics CSV against the journal keeps the weekly summary honest before the Monday checkpoint.
A quality checkpoint collapses duplicate hypotheses into a few distinct facts; reproducing the suite from a clean clone is the cheapest and most-skipped evidence box.
An in-scope asset is only the first report gate; trusted-role assumptions and absent attacker impact can independently make a clear no-submit decision.
A green suite in a dirty working tree is runnable but not portable; reproducibility requires the exact test diff and toolchain as well as the command output.
Reproducibility is its own deliverable: pin the test diff and toolchain and prove the suite runs from a clean checkout
